chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man left behind at his family's place an allowance of two thousand [dinars/dirhams] for several years, upon which is due zakat. He said: 'If he is present, then zakat is due upon him, and if he is absent, then no zakat is due upon him.'

key_terms.شَاهِدًا: Present (in this context, physically present in the location of the wealth)
key_terms.غَائِبًا: Absent (away from the location of the wealth)

ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on wealth left behind by an absent owner?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction between 'shahid' (present/aware) and 'gha'ib' (absent/unaware) highlights the Shia principle that zakat on stored wealth is contingent upon the owner's immediate possession and awareness of the nisab threshold. This ruling underscores the practical application of zakat as a purification of current wealth rather than a static tax, reflecting the juristic view that absence may imply a temporary suspension of the obligation until the wealth is effectively under the owner's control.
